title: Reuse one bounded signature list for validation and canonical ordering

masterplan.active_gate: Gate 1 — Renovation, owner-directed Genesis and general computer assistance

scope: Remove the remaining single-use _materialize_declared_sequence helper and avoid a second full selected-signature ordering container inside _selected_signatures. Preserve bounded Sequence admission, maximum cardinality refusal before indexed item access, complete declared materialization before requested-type validation, RelationSignature type validation before duplicate refusal, deterministic (source_plane, relation, target_plane) canonicalization and immutable tuple output. Reuse the existing compiler owner and selected-pruning test owner; do not add a shared admission subsystem, alternate collection contract, registry, cache, backend or second compiler.

audit.previous_behavior: Explicit requested signatures were copied through the single-use _materialize_declared_sequence helper into a tuple, validated for type and duplicates, then copied again by sorted(...) before final tuple freezing. Discover-all likewise first materialized tuple(discovered), then sorted(...) into a second full container.
audit.finding: The ordering copy was redundant. One bounded mutable list is sufficient to retain the previous requested-sequence materialization/error precedence, perform type and duplicate validation, sort canonically in place and freeze the final tuple. After GPU-83 the helper had no other owner and could be deleted rather than generalized.

production.change: Delete _materialize_declared_sequence. For requested catalogs, cache declared cardinality and index exactly that bounded cardinality into one list; for discovered signatures, create one list from the bounded discovered set. Retain full requested-item materialization before type/duplicate checks, then sort that same list in place by source_plane/relation/target_plane and freeze it once to a tuple.

focused_test.change: Extend the existing selected-pruning owner with a tracking bounded Sequence. Pin indexed declared-cardinality access, canonical order without a second module-level sorted container, removal of the retired helper, preservation of full declared materialization before requested type refusal, and explicit duplicate refusal.

semantic_invariants.bounded_admission: Explicit signatures must remain a bounded Sequence; catalogs above MAX_COMPILED_RELATIONS are refused before item consumption.
semantic_invariants.materialization_precedence: For accepted-cardinality requested catalogs, every declared index is still read before requested signature type validation, matching the previous declared-sequence materialization boundary.
semantic_invariants.type_before_duplicate: Requested values are still required to be RelationSignature records before duplicate detection is evaluated.
semantic_invariants.duplicate_refusal: Duplicate requested signatures remain an explicit ValueError.
semantic_invariants.canonical_order: Accepted signatures are still deterministically ordered by (source_plane, relation, target_plane) and returned as an immutable tuple.
semantic_invariants.source_of_truth: KnowledgeForest and FourfoldSnapshot remain authoritative; selected relation signatures remain compiler input/planning data rather than a new authority.
semantic_invariants.public_api: No public API, wire schema, benchmark schema, compatibility facade, promotion or authority contract changes.

result.summary: Selected-signature admission now owns one bounded mutable list from declared/discovered input through validation and canonical ordering, then freezes it once. The obsolete single-use materialization helper and separate sorted-container allocation are gone without relaxing admission or ordering contracts.

tauri_run.claim: No Tauri success/failure claim is made in this packet before the exact implementation-head run completes.

verification.diagnostics: CPU bitset and TypedRelationBlock validation profiles emitted by the contract workflow remain authority=diagnostic-only and claim=none.

Prefer binding the existing immutable mapping view once in bounded consumers over adding a cache or second stored mapping. Change the owner only if exact block-name lookup semantics, deterministic block order, direct-constructor validation and the regenerable-view authority boundary remain explicit; do not add a registry, cache subsystem, alternate receipt family or second compiler.
